story.title: Israel Initiates Ground Operation in Central Gaza Amid Ceasefire Tensions
story.summary: The Israeli military has launched a new ground operation in central Gaza, specifically targeting Hamas infrastructure. This operation, which occurred west of the Yellow Line, has led to the displacement of numerous Palestinians from their shelters. The military claims the action is necessary to eliminate threats to its troops, while Hamas has condemned the incursion as a violation of the ceasefire established in October 2025.

timeline_highlights.title: Israeli Strikes in Gaza Result in Seven Deaths and Destruction of Medical Warehouses
timeline_highlights.summary: Israeli military strikes in Gaza have resulted in the deaths of seven individuals and the destruction of medical supply warehouses. The Gaza Health Ministry condemned the attacks, which occurred amid ongoing uncertainty regarding a disarmament deal with Hamas. Reports indicate that the strikes targeted warehouses near a hospital, which were believed to be storing medical supplies.
key_facts: Seven individuals killed in Israeli strikes in Gaza.
Medical supply warehouses destroyed, including one at Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital.
Strikes occurred amid uncertainty over a disarmament deal with Hamas.

timeline_highlights.summary: An Israeli airstrike on the Nasser Medical Complex in Khan Younis, southern Gaza, resulted in the deaths of at least six individuals, including a doctor and a teenage boy. The attack, which occurred early on November 12, also left at least 27 others injured, according to health officials. This incident marks a significant escalation in violence amid an already fragile ceasefire in the region.

event_overview.title: About Gaza Conflict
event_overview.subject: Gaza Conflict
event_overview.summary: The Gaza conflict refers here to the war that began after Hamas and other Palestinian armed groups attacked southern Israel on 7 October 2023, killing people and taking hostages, followed by Israel's large-scale military campaign in the Gaza Strip. The conflict has involved air, ground and naval operations, rocket fire, hostage issues, severe civilian harm and displacement, humanitarian-access disputes, and international legal and diplomatic action.

facts.label: Start and status
facts.value: The current war began on 7 October 2023. Hamas and other Palestinian armed groups attacked Israel from Gaza; Israel then declared war and began military operations in Gaza. The conflict remained active during the period covered by the selected timeline.

facts.label: Main parties and setting
facts.value: The principal military parties are Israel and Hamas, alongside other Palestinian armed groups. The main theatre is the Gaza Strip, a densely populated Palestinian territory bordering Israel and Egypt; attacks and consequences have also affected Israel and the wider occupied Palestinian territory.

facts.label: Hostages
facts.value: Hamas and other armed groups abducted 251 people during the 7 October attack, making the release, recovery and treatment of hostages a central issue in ceasefire and negotiation efforts.

facts.label: Humanitarian effects
facts.value: United Nations reporting describes extensive damage to civilian infrastructure, repeated mass displacement and major constraints on humanitarian assistance in Gaza. Health facilities, water and sanitation systems, shelters, roads and aid operations have all been affected by the hostilities and access restrictions.

facts.label: International legal context
facts.value: The International Court of Justice is hearing South Africa's case against Israel under the Genocide Convention. In 2024, the Court issued provisional measures, including measures relating to Rafah and humanitarian access; such measures are interim orders and do not constitute a final ruling on the merits of the allegations.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows particular reported developments in Gaza during August and September 2026, especially strikes, casualties, medical and camp conditions, diplomacy and investigations; it does not provide a complete record of the war, negotiations, humanitarian situation or events elsewhere.

explore_lenses.title: A central-Gaza incursion disrupted civilian movement
explore_lenses.summary: The operation was reported around the Nuseirat and Al-Bureij camps, with an immediate effect on movement and on people sheltering nearby. Its reported geographic limits and duration remain unclear.

claims.text: An AFP journalist saw Israeli tanks east of Nuseirat camp; the Israeli military said it was conducting a "precise operation" west of the Yellow Line to remove a threat to troops.
COGAT told aid organizations not to move through affected areas, said the operation was near Al-Bureij and Nuseirat, and said the Salah al-Din road would be closed there.
Three Palestinians were reported killed in separate drone strikes on November 18, but AFP said it was not immediately clear whether those strikes were connected to the ground operation.

explore_lenses.label: Why is the Yellow Line central to the dispute?
explore_lenses.title: The operation crossed the ceasefire's main demarcation
explore_lenses.summary: The October 2025 ceasefire created the Yellow Line as the dividing line between Israeli-deployed and Hamas-controlled areas. Moving west of it is consequential because the line is both a military boundary and a humanitarian-access constraint.

claims.text: The ceasefire took effect on October 10, 2025; OCHA reported that Israeli forces withdrew from coastal areas to positions beyond the Yellow Line but remained deployed in areas comprising more than half of Gaza.
Israel says the November 18 operation is a response to Hamas ceasefire violations and targets Hamas infrastructure that threatens Israeli troops; Hamas calls it a flagrant breach of the ceasefire.
The UN Human Rights Office had verified 1,076 conflict-related deaths from the October 10, 2025 ceasefire announcement through July 31, 2026, including 331 near the Yellow Line.

explore_lenses.label: What steps are still pending under the ceasefire plan?
explore_lenses.title: Disarmament, withdrawal and stabilization remain stalled
explore_lenses.summary: The broader plan links Hamas disarmament, an international stabilization force, Israeli withdrawal and reconstruction. The mechanism overseeing the truce says those linked steps remain incomplete, leaving the ceasefire vulnerable to escalation.

claims.text: A UN-published Board of Peace report says the proposed roadmap requires verified decommissioning of weapons and military infrastructure, deployment of an International Stabilisation Force, and a phased Israeli withdrawal to Gaza's perimeter contingent on that verified progress.
The report said talks on the roadmap had not been finalized as of the end of its reporting period.

The Board of Peace said on November 17 that Israeli decisions on arrangements for civilian police remained pending, delaying an international stabilization force; it argued that this force is important to withdrawal, Hamas disarmament and reconstruction.

story_report.summary: Israeli tanks advanced in central Gaza on November 18 in an operation the military said targeted Hamas infrastructure and threats to its troops. An AFP journalist saw tanks east of Nuseirat camp, while the military described a “precise operation” west of the Yellow Line. The action prompted many Palestinians to flee their homes, and Hamas called it a violation of the ceasefire that took effect in October 2025. The duration, territorial scope and civilian toll directly linked to the incursion were not independently established.

sections.heading: Aid Access Near Nuseirat
sections.body: Israel’s COGAT agency told aid organizations not to move through affected areas near Al-Bureij and Nuseirat and said the Salah al-Din road would be closed in that area. The restrictions accompanied the ground operation, which was reported west of the Yellow Line while tanks were seen east of Nuseirat camp. Separately, three Palestinians were reported killed in drone strikes on November 18, though AFP said it was not immediately clear whether those strikes were connected to the incursion.

sections.heading: Ceasefire Lines and Disputed Claims
sections.body: The ceasefire took effect on October 10, 2025. OCHA reported that Israeli forces had withdrawn from coastal areas to positions beyond the Yellow Line but remained deployed in areas comprising more than half of Gaza. Israel says the operation responds to Hamas ceasefire violations and infrastructure threatening its troops; Hamas says the move is a flagrant breach. The competing assertions over violations and the alleged threat have not been independently adjudicated.

sections.heading: Unfinished Gaza Security Roadmap
sections.body: A UN-published Board of Peace report described a proposed roadmap requiring verified decommissioning of weapons and military infrastructure, an International Stabilisation Force and a phased Israeli withdrawal to Gaza’s perimeter tied to verified progress. The report said negotiations had not been finalized. The Board of Peace said pending Israeli decisions on civilian-police arrangements were delaying the proposed force, which it views as important to withdrawal, Hamas disarmament and reconstruction.

unresolved.text: Independent reporting had not established how long the operation would last, its full area of control, or a verified civilian casualty toll specifically attributable to the incursion.
No confirmed timetable was reported for finalizing the roadmap, deploying the stabilization force, completing disarmament or carrying out further Israeli withdrawal.
